articles.title: HK faces record-breaking October heat wave fueled by three key climate factors - The Standard (HK)

The Hong Kong Observatory issued a Very Hot Weather Warning at 6.45am on Wednesday as late-October temperatures soared to around 33 degrees Celsius in urban areas, with parts of the New Territories recording even higher figures.
ADVERTISEMENT
SCROLL TO CONTINUE WITH CONTENT
The temperature is expected to break the record for the latest issuance of a Very Hot Weather Warning in a year, previously set on October 19, 2024. If temperatures reach 33 degrees Celsius or above this Friday (October 23), it will also mark the hottest Frost's Descent solar term on record, surpassing the previous record of 31 degrees Celsius set in 2006.
Amos Tai Pui-kuen, professor and deputy chair of the Department of Earth and Environmental Sciences at the Chinese University of Hong Kong, explained on a radio program on Wednesday morning that this unseasonable heat wave is caused by the compounding effects of three major factors.
Amos Tai
First, the outer subsiding air currents from Super Typhoon Champi, located about 1,040 kilometers east-northeast of Manila as of 8am this morning, coupled with an anticyclone aloft over Hong Kong, led to sinking air and weakened winds. This reduced cloud cover and rainfall, allowing intense sunlight to directly heat the city.
Second, a Super El Niño altered tropical circulation patterns, creating an anomalous anticyclonic circulation over the South China Sea and the Philippines.
This suppressed convective activity and significantly weakened the northeast monsoon that typically cools the region in autumn. With the monsoon's cooling effect drastically reduced, heat easily accumulated locally. Additionally, El Niño tends to push typhoon paths further north, away from Hong Kong; however, due to extremely high sea surface temperatures, any approaching typhoon will evaporate more moisture and heat, fueling the storm's intensity.
Third, global warming has raised the overall baseline temperature. When short-term weather anomalies and climate phenomena are superimposed on a baseline that is already warped by global warming, temperatures rise significantly above historical averages.
Tai added that the impact of the Super El Niño is expected to persist through next spring, meaning Hong Kong is likely to experience an unseasonably warm winter.

articles.title: Stay Safe: CHP Urges Precautions Against Heat-Related Illnesses During Extreme Weather - 巴士的報

DH reminds public to take precautions against heat-related illnesses during very hot weather
The Centre for Health Protection (CHP) of the Department of Health (DH) today (October 21) reminded members of the public to take appropriate precautions against heat-related illnesses, such as heat cramps, heat exhaustion and heat stroke, during very hot weather.
The Centre for Health Protection. Photo source: reference image
In a high-temperature environment, excessive sweating and difficulty in heat dissipation can cause stress to the body. Members of the public should take the following precautions:
- Hydrate in a timely manner to prevent dehydration;
- Wear light-coloured, loose-fitting and breathable clothing to minimise heat absorption and facilitate perspiration and heat dissipation;
- Keep indoor areas well ventilated and maintain appropriate temperature and humidity, e.g. by opening windows or using a fan or air-conditioning;
- Avoid strenuous exercise and prolonged activities such as hiking or trekking;
- Arrange outdoor activities in the morning or the late afternoon, if possible, and bring enough water; and
- Avoid beverages containing caffeine, such as coffee and tea, as well as alcoholic beverages, which may speed up water loss through the urinary system.
In addition, infants and children, the elderly, pregnant women, individuals with chronic illnesses such as heart disease or high blood pressure, overweight people and outdoor/manual workers are more susceptible to heat stroke. These groups should pay special attention to the following:
- Infants and young children: Avoid going outside when the temperature is high. If they must go outside, adults should ensure they stay in places with moderate temperatures and good ventilation or air-conditioning. Infants and young children should never be left unattended in a confined space such as a vehicle;
- The elderly, pregnant women, individuals with chronic illnesses and overweight people: Pay close attention to health conditions and seek help as soon as possible if experiencing any abnormalities in health indicators such as blood pressure, heart rate, etc or if there are fluctuations in health conditions. Avoid going out when the temperature is high. Make sure there is good ventilation, or turn on a fan or air-conditioner to keep an appropriate temperature indoors. High temperatures can also worsen the condition of people with chronic illnesses (such as cardiovascular and respiratory diseases). Therefore, they should have an ample supply of their usual medication and keep in contact with family members, neighbours and the community. People should seek immediate help if they feel unwell.
- Outdoor/manual workers: Reschedule work to cooler hours as far as feasible. If working in a hot environment is unavoidable, provide shade where practicable and use ventilation and heat dissipation equipment. Once work has begun, gradually adjust the pace of work and take breaks in the shade to regain strength.
The DH reminded the public that heat stroke is one of the most common health risks in hot weather. Over the past five years, there have been over 200 hospital admissions due to heat stroke each year in Hong Kong, with two to five fatal cases occurring mainly during the summer months from May to September. Vulnerable groups are more susceptible to heat stroke. Symptoms include dizziness, headache, nausea, shortness of breath or confusion. In severe cases, patients may suffer from convulsions or become unconscious, which can be life-threatening if they are not cooled down and resuscitated in a timely manner.
Members of the public are also advised to pay attention to the latest weather, as well as the real-time and forecasted ultraviolet (UV) index released by the Hong Kong Observatory (HKO). When the UV index is high (6 or above), the public should note the following:
- Avoid direct sunlight exposure to the skin and the eyes;
- Apply broad-spectrum, water-resistant sunscreen liberally, with a sun protection factor (SPF) of at least 30 or higher, when participating in outdoor activities. Reapply every two hours if staying outdoors for long periods, or after swimming, sweating or towelling off;
- While using DEET-containing insect repellents for personal protection against mosquito-borne diseases, apply sunscreen before insect repellent;
If symptoms develop, such as dizziness, headache, nausea, shortness of breath or confusion, rest and seek help immediately, and seek medical advice as soon as possible.
For more health information, the public may visit the CHP's heat stroke page and UV radiation page; the HKO's Dial-a-Weather (1878 200), latest weather report and forecast, UV Index and weather information for hiking and mountaineering; and press releases of the Labour Department on precautions against heat stroke for outdoor workers and their employers when the Heat Stress at Work Warning is in force.
Hot weather in Hong Kong. Photo source: reference image
Hong Kong Customs detect drug trafficking case involving incoming air passenger at airport
Hong Kong Customs detected a drug trafficking case involving an incoming air passenger at Hong Kong International Airport today (October 21) and seized about 10 kilograms of suspected cocaine with an estimated market value of about $6 million.
A 20-year-old Mainland male passenger arrived in Hong Kong from Istanbul, Turkey, today. During Customs clearance, Customs officers found the batch of suspected cocaine inside his check-in suitcase. The man was subsequently arrested.
An investigation is ongoing.
Customs will continue to step up enforcement against drug trafficking activities through intelligence analysis. The department also reminds members of the public to stay alert and not to participate in drug trafficking activities for monetary return. They must not accept hiring or delegation from another party to carry controlled items into and out of Hong Kong. They are also reminded not to carry unknown items for other people.
Customs will continue to apply a risk assessment approach and focus on selecting passengers from high-risk regions for clearance to combat transnational drug trafficking activities.
Under the Dangerous Drugs Ordinance, trafficking in a dangerous drug is a serious offence. The maximum penalty upon conviction is a fine of $5 million and life imprisonment.
Members of the public may report any suspected drug trafficking activities to Customs' 24-hour hotline 182 8080 or its dedicated crime-reporting email account (crimereport@customs.gov.hk) or online form (eform.cefs.gov.hk/form/ced002).

articles.title: Orange alert for 4 Keralam districts amid heavy rain warning - The Hindu
articles.search_term: ("heat advisory" OR "heat action plan" OR "heat alert" OR "IMD warning" OR "IMD alert" OR "red alert" OR "orange alert" OR "yellow alert" OR "NDMA advisory" OR "cooling shelter" OR "relief measures" OR "heat compensation" OR "severe weather warning") Assam
articles.full_text:
Women workers walk through farmland in the rain in this file photo.
| Photo Credit: PTI
Parts of Keralam will continue to see heavy thunderstorms in coming days, with Bay of Bengal low-pressure systems bringing thunder, lightning, and gusty winds. A low-pressure area has formed over the southwest Bay of Bengal and adjoining Tamil Nadu coast on Wednesday. The associated cyclonic circulation will help maintain the moisture influx towards Keralam, supporting isolated to heavy to very heavy thunderstorms along the ghat regions and southern and central half of the State.
Further, another low-pressure area is expected to emerge over the southeast and adjoining east-central Bay of Bengal around October 23. As it moves northwestwards and intensifies, it could strengthen the moisture flow towards peninsular India, triggering a gradual increase in rainfall activity over Keralam from October 23, 24 and 25, with fairly widespread distribution of rain across the State.
Meanwhile, the low-pressure area over the Arabian Sea is moving away towards the Somalia coast and is therefore unlikely to have a direct significant influence on Keralam’s weather. An orange alert has been issued for Thiruvananthapuram, Kollam, Pathanamthitta, Alappuzha, and Kootayam districts on Wednesday (October 21), where very heavy rainfall is likely during the next 24 hours, according to a weather bulletin issued by the India Meteorological Department (IMD) here on Wednesday at 1 p.m., while Idukki, Ernakulam, Thrissur, Palakkad and Malappuram have been placed on a yellow alert where isolated heavy rainfall is likely.
Similarly, an orange alert has been issued for Ernakulam, Thrissur, Malappuram and Kozhikode on Thursday (October 22), and the rest of Keralam has been put on a yellow alert. Meanwhile, Ponmudi in Thiruvananthapuram recorded the highest rainfall of 14 cm during the last 24 hours ending at 8.30 a.m. on Wednesday, followed by Kollam (11 cm), Peppara in Thiruvananthapuram, Chavara in Kollam and Pampadumpara in Idukki with 9 cm each.

articles.title: Chennai school holiday, Oct 21: Schools shut in four Tamil Nadu districts as heavy rains predicted | Check IMD alert - Livemint

articles.full_text:
Chennai school holiday, Oct 21: Schools shut in four Tamil Nadu districts as heavy rains predicted | Check IMD alert The IMD issued an orange alert, predicting very heavy rainfall in Ramanathapuram, Thiruvarur, Thanjavur, Nagapattinam, Mayiladuthurau, Villupuramm Chengalpattu, Chennai and Thiruvallur. Schools in four districts of Tamil Nadu were shut on Wednesday (October 21) in the wake of the India Meteorological Department (IMD) predicting heavy rainfall in the region, local media reported. A holiday was declared for schools in Chennai, Tiruvallur, Chengalpattu and Kanchipuram districts on Wednesday, according to Dinakaran. As per the report, district collectors declared a holiday for schools due to continuous rainfall in the region. The Chennai District Collector reportedly announced that all schools in Chennai will be given a one-day holiday as a precautionary measure amid an IMD warning. Similarly, schools in Tiruvallur, Chengalpattu, and Kanchipuram districts were also declared shut on Wednesday due to incessant rains. IMD alert On Tuesday, the IMD issued yellow and orange alerts, predicting heavy rainfall in parts of Tamil Nadu and other states "due to likely formation of a low-pressure area over Southwest Bay of Bengal and adjoining Tamil Nadu coast during next 24 hours." According to the latest bulletin from the Regional Meteorological Centre on Tuesday at 1.40 pm, an upper-air cyclonic circulation that lay over the southwest Bay of Bengal off the north Tamil Nadu coast on Monday is likely to intensify into a low-pressure area over the same region during the next 24 hours. The IMD predicted, "...heavy to very heavy rainfall likely to continue over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry & Karaikal till October 26; isolated heavy rainfall likely over Lakshadweep during October 22nd-26th; Kerala and Mahe during 20th-26th October; South Interior Karnataka during 21st-24th; Coastal Andhra Pradesh & Yanam and Rayalaseema on 20th and 21st October, 2026." The IMD issued an orange alert in Ramanathapuram, Thiruvarur, Thanjavur, Nagapattinam, Mayiladuthurai, Villupuram, Chengalpattu, Chennai, and Thiruvallur. A yellow alert was issued in the remaining districts of Tamil Nadu, including Kanyakumari, Thoothukudi and Dindigul. Heavy rain is also likely in Ranipet, Kancheepuram, Kallakurichi, Tiruchirappalli, Ariyalur, Perambalur, Pudukkottai, Sivagangai, Tenkasi and Tirunelveli. However, rainfall occurred in many places across Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, and the Karaikal area during the last 24 hours, starting from Monday. Amaravathi Pudur in Sivagangai district received the highest rainfall, 9.2 cm, during the same period, followed by Tiruvadanai in Ramanathapuram, which recorded 8 cm of rain. Official sources told PTI that Chennai, which was battered by heavy downpour on Saturday night, with some areas like Parry's recording more than 30 cm of rainfall, witnessed only very moderate rains from Sunday.
